items.title: PRBench: End-to-end Paper Reproduction in Physics Research
items.title_zh: PRBench：物理研究中的端到端论文复现基准
items.summary: PRBench comprises 30 expert-curated tasks across 11 physics subfields that require agents to read a published paper, implement its algorithms from scratch and reproduce quantitative results in a sandbox. The best agent, GPT-5.3-Codex-backed OpenAI Codex, scores 34% overall, and all evaluated agents have a zero end-to-end success rate, with failures traced to formula errors, debugging gaps and fabricated output.

items.title: The Root Theorem of Context Engineering
items.summary: The paper derives a context-engineering principle from two axioms, finite context windows and quality degradation with accumulated volume: maximize signal-to-token ratio within bounded, lossy channels. It argues that append-only systems eventually exceed their effective window, that retrieval-augmented generation solves search but not continuity, and reports a 60+-session persistent architecture with a stable memory footprint.

items.title: GAAMA: Graph Augmented Associative Memory for Agents
items.title_zh: GAAMA：面向智能体的图增强联想记忆
items.summary: GAAMA builds a concept-mediated knowledge graph for agents from preserved episodes, LLM-extracted facts and higher-order reflections, and adds a post-retrieval repair layer called GRAFT. It reports 79.1% mean reward on LoCoMo-10, 4.2 points above a tuned RAG baseline.

items.title: SkyNet: Belief-Aware Planning for Partially-Observable Stochastic Games
items.title_zh: SkyNet：面向部分可观测随机博弈的信念感知规划
items.summary: SkyNet adds ego-conditioned auxiliary heads for winner prediction and rank estimation to MuZero, encouraging its latent state to retain outcome-relevant information under partial observability without explicit belief tracking. On the stochastic card game Skyjo it reaches a 75.3% peak head-to-head win rate against the baseline (+194 Elo), though it only overtakes the baseline once training throughput is sufficient.

items.title: Improving Clinical Diagnosis with Counterfactual Multi-Agent Reasoning
items.title_zh: 反事实多智能体推理改进临床诊断
items.summary: The framework applies counterfactual case editing to clinical findings and measures confidence shifts, termed the Counterfactual Probability Gap, to quantify how strongly each finding supports a diagnosis. These signals guide multi-round specialist-agent discussions, improving diagnostic accuracy over prompting and prior multi-agent baselines across three benchmarks and seven LLMs, with the largest gains on complex and ambiguous cases.

items.title: TailNLG: A Multilingual Benchmark Addressing Verbalization of Long-Tail Entities
items.title_zh: TailNLG：面向长尾实体表述的多语言基准
items.summary: TailNLG is a multilingual Data-to-Text benchmark built from Wikidata in English, Italian and Spanish that varies entity popularity. Evaluating three LLM families zero-shot, the authors find a consistent bias against long-tail entities, with lower embedding-based scores and higher model uncertainty for rare entities, which existing metrics do not reliably capture.

items.title: ATLAS-RTC: Closing the Loop on LLM Agent Output with Token-Level Runtime Control
items.title_zh: ATLAS-RTC：用 token 级运行时控制为 LLM 智能体输出闭环
items.summary: ATLAS-RTC monitors autoregressive generation step by step, detects drift from output contracts and applies biasing, masking or rollback before errors materialize. It reports 20 to 37.8 percentage-point gains in first-attempt success on structured generation and tool-calling tasks, and up to 88% lower latency when failures dominate.

items.title: graykode/abtop
items.title_zh: abtop：给 AI 编程智能体用的 htop
items.summary: abtop is a Rust tool modeled on htop that monitors AI coding agent sessions such as Claude Code and Codex CLI, tracking tokens, context-window use, rate limits and ports in real time.

items.title: ai-boost/awesome-harness-engineering
items.title_zh: awesome-harness-engineering：AI 智能体 harness 工程资源清单
items.summary: The repository is a curated list of resources for AI agent harness engineering, spanning tooling, design patterns, evaluations, memory, MCP, permissions, observability and orchestration.
